inconsistencies: Argument-typing stack: #16545 is the base, #17580 builds on it, #17493 and #17783 build on both, and #17581 builds on #17493. Review strictly in that order; the dependents' standalone scores overstated their reviewability.
#31260 (scripted-diff typed Setting) and #16545 (ALLOW_* runtime flags) reform the same argument-handling surface from two directions; the approach question should be settled once rather than per-PR.
util::Result chain: #25665 is the base; #26022 and #29700 depend on it; #25722 depends on #25665 plus #26022. #25665 carries the leverage and should be reviewed first.

#34038 and #35387 are competing solutions to the same problem (-loglevel silently ineffective, no runtime trace control). Review #34038 first since #35355 and #34730 are built on it, but a decision between the two is what unblocks the whole logging cluster.
#35322 and #35355 both replace the mutex-protected log-level map with atomic category bitmasks; this is duplicated work and only one should land.
#34778 is blocked by an unresolved concept NACK yet is the prerequisite for #29256 (kernel/wallet logging decoupling); the approach decision, not the code, is what is holding up P2 work.
#36105 (Windows exec fix) must be reviewed before #36190, which only adds tests for that fix.
#36550 supersedes #36551 and overlaps thematically with #36537; the secret-cleansing changes should be reviewed as one batch.
#36049 and #36210 both rework AutoFile/BufferedWriter error paths and will conflict; #36049 (crash fix) should go first.
#29491 and #32966 both depend on unmerged upstream libsecp256k1 work, so neither can progress on Core-side review alone.
#27409, #34603 and #36373 all concern datadir/symlink resolution; #27409 is the substantive one and the others should be checked against it.
result.notes: Four PRs were raised to P1 because they are node-wide correctness/reliability failures (data loss on reindex, process abort on write failure, out-of-bounds parser reads, shutdown deadlock) rather than ordinary bug fixes; the rest of the previously large P2 block is kept at P2. Two large dependency clusters dominate the category (argument/settings typing and logging), and within each the base PR deserves review attention ahead of its stack regardless of the dependents' individual scores.
